title: Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey on Bank Lending Practices (SLOOS), 14:00 ET — the WINTER edition, the only forward-looking one of the four
source: EST: derived from federalreserve.gov's published 2027 FOMC calendar (monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200, 164,831 bytes — the January 2027 meeting is 26-27), applied through the release-date rule the sibling sloos-2027-05-03 audited against 67 releases: the Monday five sessions after the FOMC's final day, shifted to the next business day only when that Monday is a federal holiday or the market is shut. Wednesday 2027-01-27 + 5 days = Monday 2027-02-01, which is not a federal holiday. RE-AUDITED THIS SESSION ON THE WINTER SUBSET SPECIFICALLY, where the rule is 9 for 9 (Jan-2018 through Jan-2026 editions, release dates read from each edition page's Last Update field on federalreserve.gov/data/sloos, all HTTP 200 on 2026-09-09), and all 17 January editions 2010-2026 released on a Monday with no exception. Corroborated by a calendar twin rather than by arithmetic alone: January 2027 and January 2021 are day-for-day identical months (both non-leap years beginning on a Friday) with an identical January 26-27 FOMC, and the January 2021 edition released 2021-02-01. Filed estimate because federalreserve.gov publishes no 2027 newsevents page (2027-january.htm and 2027-february.htm both returned HTTP 404 on 2026-09-09), so no primary carries either the date or the 14:00 ET slot; because the FOMC calendar it derives from carries the Fed's own caveat that 'each meeting date is tentative until confirmed at the meeting immediately preceding it'; and because this lane may not self-confirm a date it derived. Proposed 2026-09-09 by the never-assessed initial research of sloos-2027-05-03; canonical file written 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial research
notes: READ IT, DO NOT TRADE IT — and of the four 2027 editions this is the ONE to calendar, for a structural reason neither sibling had measured. SLOOS's special-question calendar is SEASONAL, and only two of the four slots are standing: the January edition carries a year-ahead outlook block (bank expectations for standards, demand and asset quality over the coming year, 'assuming that economic activity evolves in line with consensus forecasts') in 17 of 17 editions 2010-2026, no exception; the July edition carries 'Current Level of Banks' Lending Standards' in 9 of 9 since 2018, which the Fed itself introduces with 'As with all July surveys'; April and October are ad hoc, and 4 of 9 April editions ran no special questions at all. Every other SLOOS question is backward-looking — what changed over the past quarter — so THE WINTER EDITION IS THE ONLY FORWARD-LOOKING SLOOS OF THE YEAR. Its collection window is also the year's most awkward: the six January editions that publish their dates were mailed mid-December (2020-12-14, 2021-12-13, 2022-12-19, 2023-12-18, 2024-12-16, 2025-12-10) with responses due 27-32 days before release, median 31, always over the holidays. For 2027-02-01 that derives to sent ~mid-December 2026 (the Dec-2026 FOMC is 12-08/09) and DUE ~2027-01-04 — the same 01-04 the day-for-day twin Jan-2021 edition published — so the 'Outlook for 2027' is formed with the December decision in hand and roughly 23 days BEFORE the 2027-01-27 meeting whose Monday it follows. Impact LOW on this session's own measurement of the winter subset (Yahoo dividend-adjusted closes 2010-01-01 -> 2026-09-09, caches busted, 200k-iteration two-sided permutation, n=17): KRE excess vs SPY -0.336% (p=0.350 against non-SLOOS Mondays), KBE -0.169%, XLF -0.122%, SPY -0.047%, TLT -0.017%, T+1 empty. The one result that looked real is the session's cautionary tale: winter-edition ^VIX runs +7.095% against non-SLOOS Mondays at +1.756%, p=0.012 — and it SURVIVES the weekday-matched control the sibling's leg 3 introduced. Drop a single date, 2018-02-05, and it is +0.314%, p=0.486. That date is the largest one-day VIX move in the entire 2010-2026 window (+115.60%, the XIV/'VIXmageddon' session) and it is a SLOOS Monday by coincidence; leave-one-out over all 17 finds no other date whose removal breaks significance. Non-winter editions against the Monday pool run ^VIX +1.854%, p=0.986 — the Monday baseline exactly. THE RULE THIS BUYS THE CALENDAR: weekday-matching is necessary but not sufficient — on a subset of n<=20, run leave-one-out before believing anything, because one p99.9 session is enough. Attribution on 2027-02-01 is worse than at the May sibling, not better: ism-manufacturing-2027-02-01 (high, 10:00 ET) leads it by four hours, treasury-borrowing-estimates-2027-02-01 (15:00 ET, proposed in this PR) follows it by one, the FOMC decided 01-27, refunding lands 02-03 and payrolls 02-05 — the identical 10:00/14:00/15:00 triple collision on a first-trading-day-of-month Monday. Like the Beige Book it is Fed-funded and publishes through an appropriations lapse where BLS data does not. symbols: [] stays; the date is an estimate and an estimate only widens caution.
